title: AVL rotation
summary: Inserting 10, 20, 30 makes a chain; one rotation turns it back into a tree.

checkpoints.text: 10 is the root and 20 hangs on its right. Each node stores its `height`: how many levels it has, counting itself.
30 went to the right of 20. Back at node 10, the balance is 0 - 2 = -2: the right side is two levels taller. An AVL tree allows at most one level of difference.
A left rotation lifts the right child up. `y` will be the new top of this part of the tree.
10 becomes the left child of 20. The chain 10 → 20 → 30 is now a small tree with 20 on top.
`insert` returned 20, and `root` now points at it. Three levels became two, so a search needs at most two steps instead of three.
The rotation changed three pointers and two heights, and no node was copied or moved in memory. Only the arrows changed.
